summary: NetworkManager IPv4 policy override causes UDP session migration and corporate DNS resolution failures
description:
Issue summary: After a recent NetworkManager update and zero-trust agent policy rollout, some macOS and Linux clients experience mid-session UDP disruptions (gRPC/health checks, DNS over UDP) when switching between corporate Wi‑Fi and tethered cellular. Impact: internal services (metrics ingestion, service mesh healthchecks) report flapping, developer tools lose live connections, and internal DNS lookups fail intermittently for affected users. Environment: prod-us-east, zero-trust agent v5.4.1 + NetworkManager 1.38 signed package rolled 2026-03-09.

Immediate business impact: P1 — intermittent loss of internal API connections affects multiple developer teams; paging rules triggered for SREs.

High-level hypothesis: NM policy-based routing is applying an IPv4 policy override on interface change that re-annotates routes with a new nexthop/metric while the zero-trust agent updates its per-connection policy. The combination leads to UDP sockets being migrated to a different outbound path without proper conntrack/masquerade continuity, causing DNS/UDP packets to be dropped or sent out with stale source addressing.

Wanted outcome: identify root cause (agent vs NM policy parser), provide a hotfix or rollback plan, and recommend mitigations for devices in flight.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a laptop with zero-trust agent v5.4.1 installed and connected to corporate Wi‑Fi (applies default vpn route)
2) Start a persistent UDP-based session (e.g., curl --resolve to internal service using UDP DNS, or run a continuous gRPC health ping over UDP)
3) Enable tethering on phone and switch primary interface to cellular (or move out of Wi‑Fi range to force roam)
4) Observe that the UDP session drops and subsequent DNS lookups fail until agent or NM rebinds (sometimes requires toggling agent or restarting NetworkManager)
5) Repeatable on macOS (via homebrew NM shim) and Linux (Ubuntu 22.04) with the replicated package set in environment
observed_behavior: UDP sockets appear to move to a different outbound path during interface transition; some packets observed on packet captures with a source IP that doesn't match NAT translations, causing immediate drops at upstream gateway. DNS queries over UDP either get no response or responses arrive on a different interface and are discarded by the client stack.
expected_behavior: When an interface transition occurs, NetworkManager and the zero-trust agent should coordinate to preserve conntrack/NAT continuity for in-flight UDP sessions or gracefully fail over and re-establish sessions without packet loss for short roams.

investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 11:00 - Marco: Reproduced on Ubuntu 22.04 VM using nm 1.38 package. When wpa_supplicant loses AP, NM emits policy update and zt-agent immediately applies route override.
2026-03-10 12:20 - Lena Kowalski (SRE): Captures show mismatched source IPs for UDP responses; conntrack table entries being evicted or updated incorrectly during the policy change.

2026-03-10 13:05 - Marco: Verified conntrack counters spike during transition; kernel logs show 'table full' even though global conntrack max is not exhausted — suspect per-nf_conntrack bucket imbalance due to rapid replace ops.

2026-03-10 15:40 - Eng (routing team): Found recent commit in platform repo that updated policy annotation order (PR #1382) which changed how metrics and nexthops are applied when an override flag is present.

2026-03-11 09:10 - Marco: Applied local patch to delay zt-agent policy apply by 250ms after NM event — reproduction rate dropped from ~90% to ~10% in lab; indicates race between NM and zt-agent is major factor.

2026-03-11 13:30 - Lena: Performed scale test on staging with 200 clients; conntrack evictions reduced with the delay but still present under high churn. Likely need a kernel-side conntrack improvement or a smarter coordination protocol.
temporary_mitigation:
1) Roll back PR #1382 on the NM policy rollout for the affected package versions on prod-us-east.
2) As immediate client mitigation, a package-level shim will delay zt-agent applying per-connection routing for 250-500ms after interface change.
3) Increase conntrack max buckets temporarily on gateways to reduce evictions while rollout stabilizes.
next_steps: 1) Engineering to prepare a small rollback for the NetworkManager policy ordering change and coordinate a staggered redeploy to prod-us-east (owner: routing team)
2) Zero-trust team to publish a v5.4.2 agent with the 250ms debounce for policy application and provide AD/MDM config to roll it to vulnerable hosts (owner: security-agent)
3) SRE to monitor conntrack evictions and apply temporary sysctl tuning on edge NATs during the redeploy window (owner: SRE)
4) Follow-up: design a handshake between NM and zt-agent for policy transition to avoid race conditions (epic to be created if confirmed)
5) Update internal Runbook with steps and detection queries for similar events (owner: ops-docs)
resolution: Investigation in progress. Temporary mitigations validated in lab (250ms debounce) and a rollback candidate for NM policy PR identified. No full production rollback yet — awaiting approvals for staged redeploy on 2026-03-13. Post-resolution actions will include a handshake protocol design and a hardening ticket for conntrack behavior.
